newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Court removes orders on TNT trading.
newsitem.headline: Court removes orders on TNT trading.

text.p: The Federal Court on Thursday removed an order against two Australian firms which had been involved in trading in options of transport group TNT Ltd just before the announcement of a takeover bid by Koninklijke PTT of the Netherlands.

The orders sought by the Australian Securities Commission (ASC) last week applied to profits of about A$9.18 million arising from trading in the options ahead of the announcement of the bid for TNT by the Dutch telecoms and postal group.

The ASC told the court that one of the parties involved in the options trading, Cardy and Co, had given an undertaking not to dispose of the proceeds while another company, Blaironia, was no longer involved in the action.
An ASC spokeswoman said later that Cardy accounted for profits of about A$7 million and Blaironia about A$180,000.

The freeze continues on profits made by an individual investor who identified himself to brokers handling the trade as as Mark Booth. The ASC has said it cannot trace Booth, who made about A$2 million on the option dealing.
